source: Fluency Studio: Vocabulary Exercises, Weeks 1-4 (Claude Doc), revised for full coverage and recall

rules.typeTheWord: accept the key case-insensitively, ignoring extra spaces; one wrong letter in a word of 6+ letters counts as right with 'Nearly! Check the spelling: <key>'; show the key after one wrong try
rules.reviewAfterSet: every card word goes into Review as a gapped example sentence; wrong items scheduled sooner
rules.careful: show on the card in step 1 and again in feedback when the learner makes that mistake

careful.note: Careful! After get used to, use -ing: I got used to living alone (not get used to live). Spanish acostumbrarse a + infinitive is different.

match.instruction: Match each word to its meaning.

items.meaning: a time when something important changes
think about something in the past
easy to remember because it was special

text.instruction: Complete the text with words from the box. Two words are not used.
text.body: Two years ago, I (1) ___: I left Valencia and moved to Bristol. At first, life was a real (2) ___. It took me months to (3) ___ the weather! But my English (4) ___ improved, and I still (5) ___ with my friends at home.

chooseVerb.question: I ___ a risk and applied for a job abroad.
chooseVerb.reason: The collocation is take a risk (past: took).

chooseVerb.question: I've been ___ good progress since September.
I decided to ___ a change and cycle to work.
chooseVerb.reason: The collocation is make a change.

wordForms.question: My sister can never choose what to eat. She's very ___.
wordForms.reason: Indecisive means finding it difficult to decide; decisive is the opposite.

wordForms.question: Good teachers are ___: they change their plans when something isn't working.
wordForms.reason: After are we need an adjective: adaptable.

typeTheWord.instruction: Type the word or phrase from its meaning. The first letters are given.

items.meaning: start a new hobby or activity
feel sorry about something you did or didn't do
get better at something, step by step

yourSentence.prompt: Write one sentence about something that was difficult at first. Use get used to + a noun or -ing.
yourSentence.model: It took me a few weeks to get used to working from home.
yourSentence.onTargetWhen: get used to is followed by a noun or an -ing form (not the infinitive), and the sentence is about the learner

yourSentence.prompt: Write one sentence about a decision you made. Use regret or challenge.
yourSentence.model: I've never regretted learning to drive.
yourSentence.onTargetWhen: regret or challenge is used with a natural meaning, and the sentence is about the learner

careful.note: Careful! A career is your working life. A university course (Spanish carrera) is a degree: I'm doing a degree in nursing.
Careful! Intend means plan. Spanish intentar means try: I tried to call you (not I intended to call you).

match.instruction: Match each word to its meaning.

items.meaning: the last day or time when you can do something
very sure you will do something, even if it's difficult
succeed in doing something after trying hard

text.instruction: Complete the text with words from the box. Two words are not used.
text.body: My (1) ___ is to start a (2) ___ in nursing. I (3) ___ to apply for a course next spring, so this winter I'm going to (4) ___ in maths. I'm really (5) ___ to starting!

chooseVerb.question: I'm going to ___ myself a goal of reading one book a month.
chooseVerb.reason: The collocation is set (yourself) a goal.

chooseVerb.question: We'll need to finish on Thursday to ___ Friday's deadline.
chooseVerb.reason: The collocation is meet a deadline.

chooseVerb.question: Don't ___ off booking the course. Do it today!
chooseVerb.reason: Put off means delay doing something.

wordForms.question: She works very hard and wants to be a manager by 30. She's very ___.
wordForms.reason: After very we need an adjective: ambitious.

wordForms.question: Getting my driving licence was a big ___ for me.
wordForms.reason: After a big we need a noun: achievement.

typeTheWord.instruction: Type the word or phrase from its meaning. The first letters are given.

items.meaning: ask formally for a job, a course or a place
try to reach a goal, step by step
do the first thing to start something

yourSentence.prompt: Write one sentence about a goal you have for this year. Use intend to or going to.
yourSentence.model: I intend to take an English exam in June.
yourSentence.onTargetWhen: intend to + infinitive, or be going to + infinitive, for a future plan, and the sentence is about the learner

yourSentence.prompt: Write one sentence about something you're excited about. Use look forward to + a noun or -ing.
yourSentence.model: I'm looking forward to visiting my cousins in May.
yourSentence.onTargetWhen: look forward to is followed by a noun or an -ing form, and the sentence is about the learner

careful.note: Careful! Arrange means plan or organise. Spanish arreglar means fix or repair: I need to fix my bike (not arrange my bike).

match.instruction: Match each word to its meaning.

items.meaning: meet someone and tell each other your news
a problem because people understand something in different ways
uncomfortable or a little embarrassing

text.instruction: Complete the text with words from the box. Two words are not used.
text.body: Welcome to the flat! I'm sure you'll (1) ___ everyone here. We have a cleaning (2) ___: everyone has to clean the kitchen once a week. If you want to (3) ___ on Saturday, that's fine, but please tell us first. You don't have to (4) ___ anything for our Sunday dinner. And if you disagree with something, just say so (5) ___.

chooseVerb.question: We should ___ an effort to welcome new colleagues.
chooseVerb.reason: The collocation is make an effort.

chooseVerb.question: If you say you'll help, you should ___ your promise.
chooseVerb.reason: The collocation is keep a promise.

chooseVerb.question: You should ___ in touch with the organiser before Friday.
chooseVerb.reason: Get in touch means contact someone.

wordForms.question: Tom is always late and forgets things. He's very ___.
wordForms.reason: Unreliable means you can't trust someone to do what they say.

wordForms.question: It's ___ to interrupt someone when they're speaking.
wordForms.reason: Impolite means not polite; after It's we need an adjective.

typeTheWord.instruction: Type the word or phrase from its meaning. The first letters are given.

items.meaning: share many interests or opinions
visit someone at their home
plan the time and details of something

yourSentence.prompt: Write one house rule for a shared flat. Use have to, don't have to or should, and arrange or routine.
yourSentence.model: We should arrange a time to clean the kitchen together.
yourSentence.onTargetWhen: a modal (have to / don't have to / should) + infinitive is used, with arrange or routine, and the rule suits a shared flat

yourSentence.prompt: Write one sentence about someone you know. Use get on with.
yourSentence.model: I get on well with my neighbours, so we often chat in the lift.
yourSentence.onTargetWhen: get on (well) with + a person, and the sentence is about the learner's own life

careful.note: Careful! Customs, with an s, is the place at an airport where bags are checked (Spanish aduana).

match.instruction: Match each word to its meaning.

items.meaning: start a journey
new to you; you don't know it well
friendly to visitors

text.instruction: Complete the text with words from the box. Two words are not used.
text.body: Our town is a popular (1) ___ in summer. It's easy to (2) ___, because free buses are provided for visitors. You can (3) ___ of the castle, and (4) ___ food is sold at the market every Saturday. There's also an interesting (5) ___: on New Year's Day, everyone is invited to swim in the sea.

chooseVerb.question: Our flight was delayed, so we ___ our connection.
chooseVerb.reason: The collocation is miss a connection.

chooseVerb.question: We ___ light because there wasn't much room for luggage.
chooseVerb.reason: Travel light means take very little luggage.

chooseVerb.question: We ___ overnight in York before driving on.
chooseVerb.reason: Stop overnight means stay one night on a journey.

wordForms.question: Spain has a rich ___ life, with lots of festivals.
wordForms.reason: Before a noun (life) we need an adjective: cultural.

wordForms.question: On 5 November, people in Britain ___ light fireworks.
wordForms.reason: Before a verb (light) we need an adverb: traditionally.

typeTheWord.instruction: Type the word or phrase from its meaning. The first letters are given.

items.meaning: eat dishes that people from the area make
the place where you are going
travel from place to place

yourSentence.prompt: Write one sentence about a place you know. Use the passive (is / are + past participle) and local.
yourSentence.model: Fresh fish is sold at the local market every morning.
yourSentence.onTargetWhen: the present simple passive (is / are + past participle) is used, with local, about a real place

yourSentence.prompt: Write one sentence to tell a visitor about a custom or tradition in your town.
yourSentence.model: In my town, visitors are invited to join the summer festival in August.
yourSentence.onTargetWhen: custom or tradition is used correctly, with a clear meaning, about the learner's own town
